title: AI Mediation of Economic Decisions: A Registered Forecast, a Conditional Valuation, and a Statement of Burden (EA-MEDIATED-SHARE-01 v0.3)
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: A forecast registered in advance so it can be checked and found wrong. It separates three overlapping events (AI-influenced, AI-referred, agent-executed), sets the measured US retail base against the McKinsey and Bain 2030 forecasts and shows the two cannot be compared, estimates AI-referred dollar share with its equal-order-value assumption stated, publishes a conditional valuation as a curve with the unmeasured term left as a free axis, specifies the trial that would measure it, and states where the evidentiary burden sits. Eight resolution criteria carry named sources and check dates.
substrate: AI-assisted (substrate) — drafted in working session with Claude (Anthropic) under MANUS direction. Version 0.3 records its six repairs to v0.2 in the text, including one withdrawn finding that rested on a summariser's gloss rather than the source.
methodology: Every figure is marked measured, estimated or assumed, with source and date. Measured inputs are taken from US Census, Adobe Digital Insights, Conductor, Similarweb and the Attrifast cohort as published; the McKinsey scope question was settled by reading the source page rather than a summary of it. Estimates chain named measurement populations and state their assumptions. The valuation is published as a function of a free parameter rather than a figure.
falsification_conditions: Resolution criteria 1–8 in section 9, each with a named source and check date; a source that stops publishing resolves the item UNRESOLVED. Section 10 states the outcomes that would make the document wrong in informative ways, including AI-referred dollar share below 1 percent at end of 2026 and any vendor publishing entity-resolution accuracy by field with a stated rubric and open sample.
axn_reading: Search -> Alarm -> Proof -> Alarm -> Origin -> Transmutation
wiki_article: EA-MEDIATED-SHARE-01 is a registered forecast on how much economic decision-making AI systems mediate, issued on 2026-09-20 so that its figures can later be checked against named sources. It distinguishes three overlapping events — a buyer consulting an AI system, a session referred from an AI surface, and a transaction completed by an agent — and insists that figures counting different events cannot be summed. Against the US Census retail base it shows that the McKinsey and Bain 2030 forecasts differ by a factor of 1.8 to 3.3 and cannot be compared, because only one defines its scope. It estimates AI-referred dollar share at 3 to 8 percent by end of 2026 under an equal-order-value assumption it labels unverified, and agent-executed share at 5 to 15 percent by 2030. Its valuation is a curve rather than a number: value equals encounters times the measured change in entity-resolution accuracy times an unmeasured probability of outcome change times margin, with that probability left as an axis. It specifies a matched, randomised trial against conventional structured data, and argues that no public corpus other than the Capture Registry holds dated, transcript-preserved observations of entity resolution across surfaces.
